podcast.title: ABBA's Non-Affiliation
podcast.body: ABBA was not considered part of the singer-songwriter movement that was active in the mid-1970s, further distinguishing their musical style. "they were not part of the singer songwriter movement."

podcast.title: Ben Howard's Style
podcast.body: Ben Howard is described as a typical "singer with a guitar" in the singer-songwriter tradition, who has achieved considerable success in the UK, with a style comparable to artists like Bon Iver (referred to as Curnivar net in the transcript). podcast.title: Part of Alt Rock Umbrella
podcast.body: Singer-songwriters whose style didn't conform to the mainstream view of rock were among the "new fresh, strange and fascinating sounds" discovered under the umbrella of Alternative Rock in the 1990s. "Things like Goth, Industrial, Shoegays, Lofi, even singer songwriters that didn't fit the mainstream's view of Rock."

podcast.title: Prominence in 2010s
podcast.body: The 2010s saw a rise in prominence for individual singer-songwriters, duos, or small combos, often utilizing acoustic guitars, mandolins, banjos, ukuleles, and accordions. "What kind of music was big? Well, acoustic guitars, mandalins, banjos, ukulele's, accordions, played by a new generation of individual singer-songwriters, duos, or small combos."

podcast.title: The Troubadour as the Heartbeat of the Movement
podcast.body: The Troubadour is perhaps best known as the "heartbeat" of the singer-songwriter movement of the early 1970s. Artists like James Taylor and Jackson Browne, writing introspective and autobiographical songs, found their footing and audience there, tapping into a 70s desire for authenticity. "The Trubidor showcased a wide variety of talent, but is perhaps best known as kind of the heartbeat of the singer songwriter movement of the early 70s."
